version.changelog:
- Removed the skill-card.md file.
- Minor documentation updates in SKILL.md; no user-facing functionality changes documented.

llm.summary: This is a clearly documented self-hosted speech tool, but users should only point it at a trusted Talkies server because audio, text, and voice samples are sent there.

dimensions.detail: Network access, Docker, ffmpeg/curl usage, and model storage are proportionate for a self-hosted speech service, though public deployments require auth, TLS, and careful network exposure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses documented Docker commands, model downloads, optional GPU access, and optional bearer auth; no hidden install behavior or persistence outside the described container/data volume was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly warns that data goes to the configured TALKIES_URL, that URL downloads happen server-side, that staged files are shared, and that agents should only manage files they staged in the current workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Server-side staged files, downloaded URL cache, model files, and custom voices persist by design and are disclosed, with cleanup and access-control guidance provided.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The declared ASR/TTS purpose matches the documented capabilities: transcription, speech generation, voice cloning, URL fetching, MCP tools, Docker setup, and server-side file staging.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you will use a Talkies server you run or explicitly trust. Prefer localhost or HTTPS, enable TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN for any shared or exposed server, avoid sending sensitive text/audio to untrusted hosts, clean up staged files, and only use voice cloning with the speaker's consent.
llm.findings:
[E1] expected: The TTS examples send input text to TALKIES_URL, which is expected for speech synthesis and is prominently disclosed as data leaving the host.
[E1] expected: The cloned-voice example uses a reference voice on the configured server; this is purpose-aligned and accompanied by consent and trusted-server warnings.
[E1] expected: The workflow example again transmits text to the configured service; the confidentiality risk is real but documented rather than hidden or purpose-mismatched.
